properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/14/2024 to QUESTA PETRO CO in East Huntingdon Township, Westmoreland county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: QUESTA PETRO CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/14/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8191186
Permit API: 129-26032
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: East Huntingdon Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/14/2024
Comments: On June 14, 2024 the Department conducted a Routine Inspection of the Joseph A Negri 1 well located in East Huntington Township, Westmoreland County. During a previous inspection (IR 3723492) the Department observed a drum on site with a Methanol label on it. At that time the Department requested the operator provide information by 3/29/24 on what exactly is in the drum and what it is being used for, the Department also requested that the Operator remove all equipment not necessary for production. The Department has not received a response from the Operator in regards to this site.At the time of this inspection, the well site was exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues observed. A well tag with all required information posted on it was fixed to the wellhead. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the wellhead. Some production equipment onsite that appeared to be in production due to the gauge attached to it had an open pipe close to the ground. A soil conductivity reading was taken at the edge of the well site in some vegetation as a background (0.0074 mS) and then a reading was taken directly next to the piping (0.409 mS) and then a little further back from this piping (0.382 mS). The production tank also had some wet marks coming from the top of the tank and the wet marks can be seen going down the tank towards the ground in areas. Soil conductivity readings were taken at the base of the production tank below areas where the wet marks were observed on the tank (0.1483 mS and 0.1405 mS). The drum of methanol was observed to still be on site, not in secondary containment and fluid can be seen sitting at the top of it with air bubbles forming from what may be a small hole or crack in the top of the barrel. Soil conductivity readings were taken at the base of the drum (0.096 mS), as well as in the fluid sitting at the top of the drum (0.620 mS).The soil conductivity readings taken near the open pipe and at the base of the production tank are elevated in comparison to the background soil conductivity reading and subjugate that there is some sort of release contaminating the soil in both areas. The reading at the base of the Methanol drum is comparable to the background, but the fluid sitting at the top and the air bubbles seen indicate that there may be a leak at the top of the drum which currently has the potential to reach the ground. While onsite, the Department spoke with Dave Lindahl of Mountain View to let him know about the elevated readings by the production equipment and production tank and informed him about the possible hole at the top of the Methanol Drum. The Department recommended the drum be removed or put in secondary containment as soon as possible and recommended they determine how the two leaks occurred, stop them, remove all contaminated soil, replace it with new top soil, and seed/mulch. Dave stated that someone would be onsite on 6/17/24 to begin working on all of this. The Department is recommending the Operator either remove this drum or put it within secondary containment by COB June 28, 2024. Based on todays inspection, violations shall be issued at this time for failure to remove production equipment not currently in use and for a release from production equipment.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) completed an administrative inspection on Repsol's DCNR 587 02-003 10H well (117-22101) located in Ward Township, Tioga County on 7/27/2022. The inspection was completed in order to summarize sample results from a sample collected during the 7/5/2022 inspection (inspection record # 3394821). On 7/5/2022, the DEP conducted an inspection of the DCNR 587 02-003 well site and discovered elevated electrical conductivity fluids on the pad surface. Field readings from numerous puddles located all over the pad surface ranged from ~1.7mS/cm to ~12.78mS/cm. A puddle located in front of the produced water temporary storage containers held on the northern edge of the pad surface was field measured at ~12.78mS/cm. Sample 0983-318 was collected from that puddle on 7/5/2022. Final sample results for sample 0983-318 were received by the DEP on 7/23/2022. The DEP's analytical results are attached as photos and as a file. Additional information regarding the initial inspection from 7/5/2022 can be found in inspection record # 3394821. The operator was notified of the findings from the 7/5/2022 inspection report via phone on the same day. The operator explained that a water truck would be in route to recover the fluids found. Based on the findings of the 7/5/2022 inspection report (inspection record # 3394821) and based on the analytical sample results found in this report, violations of the following are cited against API # 117-22101 at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)35 P.S. 691.402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301

Violation ID: 855652
Permit API: 081-20566
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cogan House Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-07-15
Comments: On July 15, 2019, Department representative Brad Kline and Jared Jacobini conducted an investigation of production fluid leak at the Range Resources Bobst Mountain 18-23H Pad. The Department met with Kirby Steck with Range Resources, he stated that upon excavation of the dump line of the GPU, they did not find a rock guard around the line. Range Resources is suspecting that this caused the hole in the dump line. Range Resources estimated about 1.25 barrel of production fluid had leaked out of the line. At the time of inspection, Range Resources had excavated down to the dump line but were waiting on another piece of equipment to continue removing the impacted soil. A 10'x15' area of impact had been excavated but more soil beneath the dump line needs to be removed. The impacted soil is being placed into covered 25 yard roll back dumpsters. At the time about 2.5 dumpsters had been filled. The release of production fluid caused by the hole in the dump line is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), 78a.54, and Section 301 of the Solid Waste Management Act. Due to the volume of production fluid leaked, remediation under Act 2 is required under 78a.66(c).

Comments: This inspection has been conducted in response to an anonymous complaint submitted to the Department on July 29, 2020. The complaint alleged that a poly brine tank, associated with Well #: 019-21522(Haugh 1), was damaged, and has been leaking brine on to the ground surface for some time. These allegations have been verified in the field. A large crack exists on the eastern facing side of the tank. Fluid seems to have drained at a slow but steady rate from above the crack. It is unclear how much fluid has drained from the tank over time. An earthen containment exits around the tank. The leaked fluid, however, seems to be traveling directly down through the soil. It is not clear as to where the fluid is migrating to beyond the contained area. There are no clear outlets in the area immediately beyond the containment. It is recommended that the tank be repaired or replaced to comply with regulatory requirements associated with petroleum brine management and storage.

Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected. ¿¿ VIOLATION:78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS – MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well. ¿¿ VIOLATION: 78.81(a)1 - CASING AND CEMENTING – GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to allow for effective control of the well at all times At this time, the Department is requesting an investigation into the possible source of methane to be conducted by the operator. Comments: On August 27, 2025, the Department met on-site with the Operator and Moody and Associates to assess the access road culvert inlet. Accompanying me today is Lisa Raffle (Diversified), Glenn Wilson (Diversified), Jessie Bobrzynski (Moody), and Jona Stoskey (Moody).Due to the approximate specific conductivity threshold of 4.00 mS (according to Moody and Associates), the stained area observed in IR 4040776 on the access road will not be assessed. During today's on-site inspection/meeting, specific conductivity of the soil under the rip rap of the access road's culvert inlet was measured by the Department and Moody. Moody utilized their own specific conductivity probe/meter as well as a probe/meter supplied by Diversified. The Department utilized its own specific conductivity probe/meter. All three specific conductivity probes/meters were calibrated on-site prior to the inspection/meeting.Upon arrival to the culvert inlet, Lisa Raffle of Diversified informed the Department that she took readings of specific conductivity following the Department's latest on-site inspection (IR 4040776), to which she did not observe readings anywhere near as high as the Department did. The Department asked Raffle where the readings were taken from, to which Raffle indicated it was from the excavated area (Photo 2) within the culvert ditch. This small excavated area is observed to be upslope of the culvert and just downslope of the access road. The Department clarified that each of the specific conductivity readings for this inlet that were probed by the Department in previous on-site inspection were probed directly in front of the culvert inlet.Specific conductivity readings were probed by Moody and the Department in front of, under, and on the sides of the culvert inlet. Readings were observed to be 'Or' (Out of Range) or above 20.0 mS underneath and to the right (South) of the culvert. Glenn Wilson (Diversified) promptly removed approximately one and a half 5-gallon buckets of impacted material from this area (Photo 3).Following the removal of this material, Moody probed again and recorded readings between 6.0-10.0 mS underneath the culvert inlet. At this time, Diversified and Moody jointly decided to halt removal of material and collect a soil sample of the soil that was producing the 6.0-10.0 mS readings. The Department also collected a soil sample (SAC 960) from this location following Moody's collection. Based on today's inspection, all issued violations remain outstanding.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 911089
Permit API: 015-23648
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/18/2021
Comments: On 03/18/2021, Department of Environmental Protection representative John Ciccone (Water Quality Specialist) conducted an inspection at Chesapeake Appalachia LLC’s (CALLC) MAGGIE location in response to a spill notification (Complaint ID # 355355). Eric Hottenstein (CALLC HSE Supervisor) reported the release at 0700 hours on 03/18/2021. Mr. Hottenstein’s initial report stated that he was notified that an estimated 100 gallons of Blue Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF), an additive for diesel fuel, was spilled onto the western side of the pad surface. According to the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) on DEF, the substance is a mixture of 67.5% water and 32.5% urea by weight (photo # 9). The spill occurred when a 400-gallon tote of DEF was punctured by a forklift while repositioning the tote onto containment. Fluid that was pooled on the pad surface was vacuumed up and impacted soils were excavated. Excavated soils were placed within containment. I arrived onsite at 1051 hours. The weather was 43 degrees with steady rainfall. CALLC crews were present onsite and preparing for stimulation operations, scheduled to begin today (03/18/2021). I checked in with Brent Thomas (CALLC Safety Manager) to announce my presence and in order to be guided to the release location. I observed 2 separate containments, each approximately 12 feet x 12 feet in dimension, that excavated soils were staged within (photo # 1, 2). Excavated soils were covered with tarp, and containments had berms present. A vacuum truck was parked at the location of release at the time of my arrival (photo # 3). Mr. Thomas instructed to truck to move so I could gather observations. According to photographs of the initial release, an area of approximately 20 feet x 20 feet was impacted (photo # 15). During the time of this inspection, the area was covered puddles and was not covered with containment (photo # 4). No staining on the pad surface or odors were noted at this time. Comments: On March 19, 2026, the DEP conducted a Follow Up Inspection in response to IRs 4157087, 4157136, 4157162, 4157480, and 4157532. This inspection is separated into 2 inspection reports and discusses 8 observed culverts along the access road as well as any observed erosion and sedimentation issues along the access road. This Inspection Report is Inspection 1 of 2 and assesses Culverts 1-5. All associated violations discussed in both inspection reports are being issued/continued in just this inspection.A COA with the DEP was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. At this time, a rig was on site and plugging operations have commenced.During IRs 4157087/4157136/4157162, the DEP recommended the operator install controls in accordance with the construction sequence and the E and S plan and redline the site plans to appropriately match on-site field changes.During IRs 4157480/4157532, the DEP recommended the operator install CFS along the access road in all sections of E and S off of the access road and above each culvert inlet and outlet, as well as gravel the access road at all culvert crossings in accordance with the E and S plan. The DEP recommended the operator install orange construction fence along the access road near the seep and wetland identified near the culvert 4 inlet and past culvert 5. The DEP recommended the operator restore the roadside ditch at seep.At the time of this inspection, the E and S plan was present in the on-site mailbox at the beginning of the access road. The DEP did not observed any redlining on site plans to depict and appropriately match on-site field changes (Photo 2). The DEP also did not observe the RCE to be installed at the beginning of the access road as depicted on the plans (Photo 1). The access road was also observed to still not be graveled by the operator despite the E and S plan calling for the road to be "graveled as necessary". CFS was observed to be installed at an area where erosion and sedimentation off the access road was previously noted to be located before culvert 1.Observations obtained during today's inspection at culvert crossings 1-5 are as follows:Culvert 1 crossing - culverted for a roadside ditch (Photos 4-7): The outlet still appears to be block. CFS was observed at both the inlet and outlet, however, the CFS at the outlet is improperly installed as complete surface contact to the ground was not observed. Culvert 2 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 8-9): Outlet still appears to be blocked. CFS was observed to be installed and functioning properly at both the inlet and outlet. Culvert 3 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 10-13): The inlet to this culvert appears to still be blocked. CFS was installed at both the inlet and outlet of this culvert, however, the CFS at the inlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. No sediment was observed to be entering the stream at this time.Culvert 4 crossing - culverted for roadside ditch (Photos 14-17): CFS was observed to be installed at both the inlet and outlet of this culvert, however, the CFS at the inlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. Culvert still appears to not be receiving water due to operator disturbing channel and causing water to be diverted further down access road. The disturbed channel still appears to be carrying fine sediment towards the stream at culvert 5, however no sediment was observed entering the stream due to the second half of the channel going subsurface with the entry point into the stream unseen (Photos 18-20).Culvert 5 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 21-24): CFS was observed to be installed at both the inlet and outlet of this crossing, however, the CFS at the outlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. No sediment was observed to be entering the stream at this time.

Inspection Date: 5/17/2021
Comments: The DEP completed an administrative inspection on Tilden Bradford's Nichols 1H well (API 015-21167) located in Smithfield Township, Bradford County on 5/17/2021. The inspection was completed in order to summarize sample results from a sample collected during the 4/26/2021 inspection (IR #3182275). On 4/26/2021, I inspected Tilden Bradford's Nichols A well site and discovered elevated electrical conductivity (EC) puddles on the pad surface, outside of containment. Elevated EC puddles were field measured utilizing an Oakton PCSTestr 35 and ranged in EC from ~2.1mS/cm to ~4.87mS/cm. A sample for standard analysis code (SAC) 942 was collected on 4/26/2021 from a puddle field measured at ~4.87mS/cm. The sample was submitted to the DEP Laboratory in Harrisburg, PA on 4/27/2021 and the final sample results were reported on 5/15/2021. The DEP's analytical sample results are attached as photos and as a file. Additional information regarding the inspection can be found in inspection record #3182275. The operator later provided an email determining that the elevated EC water must have been from a water truck that had a spill in the offload area and then drove through it and onto the pad as they left. Remediation began as soon as the operator was notified. Based on the sample results of 0983-202 and the findings from inspection record #3182275, violations of the following are now cited against API # 015-21167: 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a) 35 P.S. 6018.301

Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 995320
Permit API: 051-23285
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Dunbar Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/11/2023
Comments: On May 11th 2023, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Nelson 2 OG Well. The findings were as follows:At the time of the inspection, the well appeared to be equipped for production. The well posting was present at the time of the inspection.The access road appeared to be stable with no signs of erosion or sedimentation issues. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. There were erosion and sedimentation issues onsite due to the pump jack actively releasing fluid onto the ground. There were observed leaks and discharge on the ground and around the wellhead. The Department observed the pump jack is actively releasing a fluid (where the pump jack enters the wellhead) to the ground. This active release is causing erosion to occur in the adjacent field. The Department recommends that the Operator remediate the area as necessary in accordance with the Department's Spill Policy. The Department requests the operator provide a quantity of what was released, what specific fluids were released, and when and how the release occurred. Soil conductivity readings were taken at 2 points on the site of the stained soil. The soil conductivity readings were out of range (above 20.00mS). Soil samples were also taken at three points(see photos 9,10,11). Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued. Additional violations maybe forthcoming pending further review of sampling results.

Permit API: 111-20223

Comments: On July 23, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management Inc's Neilan 1 gas well site located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4209208, where violations were continued for broken and corroded piping causing a release, as well as the issuance of new violations for inaccurate information on the well tag, and failure to remove production equipment not currently in use from the gas well site.Accompanying on today's inspection is DEP ET Rosie Wise.At the time of this inspection, site conditions appear to be unchanged from IR 4209208, and to date, a Notice of Violation Operator response has yet to be received.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the gas wellhead with all required information posted on it, however the well tag does not appear to updated and the phone number listed on the tag is not in service. Violations are being continued at this time for having inaccurate information on the well tag/posting. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the gas wellhead. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a small production tank adjacent to the gas wellhead, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this tank. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site. The tank on the left was observed to be green and the tank on the right was observed to be a faded green color. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the green (left) production tank on site, however, the faded green (right) production tank was observed to have several corroded pipes connected to it. Towards the top of the faded green (right) production tank, the Department observed an area where severe corrosion caused piping to break off. This broken pipe was observed to be on the ground at the base of the production tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this broken pipe, from the other corroded pipes still connected to the production tank, or the production tank at the time of this inspection. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the area at the base of the faded green production tank ((3.80 mS and Over Range (>12mS)) and adjacent to the broken corroded pipe (0.329 mS). These conductivity readings were compared to a background soil conductivity reading of 0.181 mS collected upslope and away from the release area. The soil conductivity readings in the release area are elevated compared to background subjugating that the release from the back of the production tank on the right has yet to be remediated. Violations are being continued at this time for the release from the production tank.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed production equipment connected to a meter box, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production equipment or meter box. Inside the Meter Box, the Department observed production paper that was dated 10/27/2023. A pile of pipes was observed on the ground adjacent to the meter box and production equipment. Violations are being continued at this time for failure to remove production equipment not in use from the gas well site. The Department is again requesting the Operator provide the Department with a Notice of Violation Operator response within 14 days of the receipt of this inspection report.Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from corroded and broken piping, inaccurate information on the well tag, and failure to remove production equipment not currently in use from the gas well site is to remain outstanding at this time.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Stepped Pressure Build Up Tests (SPBUTs) being performed on all (5) wells on the Hunter pad., the Hunter 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H. These SPBUTs are being performed to assess the recent remedial work, CET (Casing Expansion Tool), deployment performed on all (5) Hunter wells production casing strings. This is the 6th post CET deployment PBUTs being performed on the 21HC, 22HC and the 23HC and the 1st PBUTs performed on the 5H and 6H since Perf. and Squeeze ops were completed on 5/16/22. - All (5) wells on the pad are in production. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a production tank via 2" common vent line. Comments: On 06/14/2022 I conducted a routine inspection of the Gray Todd and Gray 5 40 OG well. The owner of this well is listed as Titus Energy. The tank battery approx 200 feet to the south of this pad has brine seeping out of the southwest corner of the tank impoundment. The SW corner of the impoundment was void of vegetation in what is an area about 40 feet by 60 feet and had an abundant amount of hoof prints around this corner. Using a conductivity probe, readings in one location were over range for the meter. Other readings in this corner ranged from 13.35 mS/cm to 4.79 mS/cm. Readings at this level are indicative of a release. Browns Run is approx 630 feet down gradient from the tank battery. The tank battery is located on FS 160D at the bottom of road. It is unclear how much brine has been released. It is currently unclear if the brine has made its way into Browns Run.
